Title: Diagnosis of test `testIndexOfAnyBut_StringStringWithSupplementaryChars()`

Details:
1. The failing test calls `StringUtils.indexOfAnyBut` with `str = CharU20000 + CharU20001` and `searchChars = CharU20000`. These constants likely represent Unicode supplementary characters (characters outside the BMP that require surrogate pairs in UTF-16).
2. The method `indexOfAnyBut(String str, String searchChars)` implementation uses `str.length()` to control the iteration over characters and uses `charAt(i)` to get each character.
3. However, `charAt(i)` and `length()` treat the string in UTF-16 code units, not Unicode code points.
4. Supplementary characters are represented by two UTF-16 code units (a surrogate pair). Thus, `charAt(i)` handles part of a surrogate pair as a char, not as a full code point.
5. The method checks each UTF-16 code unit of `str` against the UTF-16 code units in `searchChars` with `searchChars.indexOf(ch)`.
6. Since supplementary characters in `searchChars` are also surrogate pairs, `searchChars.indexOf(ch)` only matches one half of the surrogate pair at a time.
7. The method returns the index based on code units, so it may return unexpected results when supplementary characters are involved.
8. The test expects the method to correctly handle supplementary characters as single characters/code points and return the index `2`. This implies the test expects iteration by code points, not code units.
9. The root cause is the method `indexOfAnyBut` not accounting for supplementary characters properly. It uses `charAt(i)` and `length()` instead of handling full Unicode code points (e.g., using `codePointAt` and `offsetByCodePoints`).

This causes incorrect behavior when the input strings contain supplementary characters.

Next, the best method to fix is `StringUtils.indexOfAnyBut(String, String)` to handle supplementary characters correctly.
org.apache.commons.lang3.StringUtils.indexOfAnyBut(java.lang.String,java.lang.String)
